subject.title: [Slack] Agent lacks visibility into own channel messages from DM sessions

question: Should Slack DM/main sessions recall outbound channel activity through broad same-agent session tools, or through a narrower outbound-only activity store?
rationale: Current main offers broad opt-in same-agent transcript access, but the requested default continuity crosses user and channel privacy boundaries and requires explicit retention and authorization policy.

options.title: Scoped activity ledger
options.body: Persist only the agent’s own outbound Slack activity with bounded retention, redaction, account/team isolation, and destination-aware authorization.

options.title: Document agent visibility
options.body: Use `tools.sessions.visibility: agent` with `sessions_list` and `sessions_history` as the trusted-workspace solution, accepting access to broader same-agent transcripts.

options.title: Preserve current isolation
options.body: Keep tree-only visibility and require deliberate shared-memory writes for cross-context continuity.

recommendation.title: Scoped activity ledger
recommendation.body: Persist only the agent’s own outbound Slack activity with bounded retention, redaction, account/team isolation, and destination-aware authorization.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior issue review and recent routing/outbound history place this product and privacy decision closest to steipete.
